orders.reason: Chronic liver disease of unknown cause with rising transaminases, fatigue, abdominal pain

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Four-month diabetes check, first since metformin. Taking metformin 500 bid, colesevelam 3 tabs bid, ezetimibe, D3 in the morning away from colesevelam. No hypoglycemia symptoms.

New since the fall: tired most days, since around October -- he first put it down to year-end at work, but it has not let up over the holidays. Intermittent abdominal pain, hard for him to localize, comes and goes, no relation to meals he can find, no vomiting, no black stools. Joints are stiffer than they used to be, especially mornings, and the acetaminophen does less. No fevers, no weight change he has noticed, no rash.

O: vitals per flowsheet, weight stable. Tired-appearing but comfortable. Sclerae anicteric. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nondistended, no guarding. Hands: no swelling or warmth today. Feet: skin intact, pulses 2+, monofilament sensation intact bilaterally, no calluses.

A/P
1. Type 2 diabetes: A1c today, urine albumin/creatinine. Continue metformin.
2. FH on ezetimibe + colesevelam: lipids today, about 3 months on colesevelam as cardiology asked.
3. Fatigue, abdominal pain, joint stiffness x ~3 months, in a man with chronic liver disease nobody has explained: CMP, CBC, TSH today. Regardless of results, I want gastroenterology to look at the liver properly -- referral placed.
4. Shingrix #2 today.
RTC after GI, or sooner if symptoms worsen.

documents.title: Referral to Gastroenterology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Reason for referral: chronic liver disease of undetermined cause, now with symptoms.

50 yo man, never drinks. Transaminases mildly raised since at least 2023 (AST 66, ALT 79 then; stable through 2025). Prior practice evaluation not available to us. Now about 3 months of fatigue, intermittent abdominal pain and worsening joint stiffness. Type 2 diabetes diagnosed 9/2025 on metformin. Heterozygous FH on ezetimibe and colesevelam (atorvastatin myopathy 2021). S/p cholecystectomy 2018. Brother with cirrhosis of unknown cause.

Labs from today to follow.

Allergies: atorvastatin (myalgia, CK rise); sulfa (rash).

Please evaluate. Thank you.

documents.title: January labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Viktor,

- A1c 6.6, down from 7.0. Good.
- LDL 158, down from 185 since colesevelam. Still above where we'd like it; I'll copy cardiology.
- Thyroid, blood counts and kidney function normal. Urine protein normal.
- Liver enzymes: AST 92 and ALT 105, higher than they have been. Bilirubin and albumin normal.

The liver numbers are part of why I want gastroenterology involved. Their office should call you; tell us if they haven't in a couple of weeks.

Your PCP

documents.title: GI scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called -- GI's first new-patient opening is 4/21. Asked if we could get him in sooner. Called GI office, no earlier slots, added to their cancellation list. Labs and referral note faxed to GI again at their request. Pt aware; told him to call us if he feels worse before then.

documents.title: GI appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw GI yesterday. He examined me and said my liver is enlarged and asked whether anyone had commented on my skin color -- apparently I have a bronze tint. Blood work there showed iron very high, ferritin 2500. He thinks it's hemochromatosis and that it could explain the liver, the joints, maybe even the diabetes. Sending a gene test and an ultrasound next week. He said a letter will come to you. Honestly a little rattled -- my brother's liver comes to mind.

documents.title: RE: GI appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me right away. That fits the picture, and if the gene test confirms it, the good news is that it is treatable -- removing blood regularly brings the iron down, and that protects the liver and other organs. Let's get the ultrasound and gene test done, and once GI's plan is set I'd like to see you in the office. Your brother's doctors may want to know about this too; we can talk about that when I see you. Call anytime before then.

reports.text:
OUTSIDE IMAGING -- copy to primary care.
EXAM: Ultrasound abdomen, complete.
INDICATION: Iron overload, suspected hemochromatosis; hepatomegaly on exam.
COMPARISON: None.
FINDINGS: The liver is enlarged, measuring 19.5 cm in craniocaudal length at the midclavicular line. Contour is smooth. No focal hepatic lesion. Portal vein patent with normal hepatopetal flow. No intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation; common duct 5 mm, within normal limits after cholecystectomy. Gallbladder surgically absent. Spleen 11.2 cm, normal. Pancreas visualized portions unremarkable. Kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. Abdominal aorta normal caliber. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Hepatomegaly with smooth contour and no focal liver lesion. Normal spleen. No ascites. Status post cholecystectomy.

documents.title: Outside abdominal ultrasound received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Outside ultrasound report (ordered by GI, cc PCP) received and scanned. Routed to PCP for review.

documents.title: Gene test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: GI called today. Two copies of the C282Y gene, so hemochromatosis is confirmed. Weekly blood removal starts next Tuesday at the infusion center, a pint each time, until the ferritin gets down to 50-100. They said no iron pills or vitamin C supplements and no raw shellfish. My vitamin D is ok right? Also the ultrasound -- GI said the liver is big but nothing else concerning. Can I book with you after I've had a couple of sessions?

documents.title: RE: Gene test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks Viktor. I saw the ultrasound too -- enlarged liver, smooth, no spots or lesions, spleen normal. Vitamin D is fine to keep. I've added hereditary hemochromatosis to your problem list. Front desk will book you for the week of May 18.

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology and hepatology. Date of service 4/21/2026; genotype addendum 5/4/2026. Received 5/14/2026.

Dear colleague,

Thank you for referring Mr. Michaud, a 50-year-old man with long-standing transaminase elevation of undetermined cause.

He describes about six months of fatigue, abdominal pain and joint stiffness. Type 2 diabetes was diagnosed last September. He is a lifelong nonsmoker and has never used alcohol. His mother has type 2 diabetes; his father had an MI at 42 and hyperlipidemia; a brother has cirrhosis of unknown cause. Prior cholecystectomy. Medications: ezetimibe 10 mg daily, colesevelam 1875 mg twice daily, metformin 500 mg twice daily, acetaminophen 500 mg every 6 hours as needed, vitamin D3 2000 units daily. Allergies: atorvastatin (myopathy, CK rise); sulfonamides (rash).

Examination: bronze discoloration of the skin. The liver is enlarged. Abdomen otherwise soft.

Laboratory (4/21): ferritin 2500 ng/mL (24-336); transferrin saturation 85% (20-50); AST 98 U/L; ALT 110 U/L; fasting glucose 160 mg/dL.

Impression: hereditary hemochromatosis with arthropathy, with iron-related liver disease. The skin finding, hepatomegaly, joint symptoms and new diabetes all fit.

Addendum 5/4: HFE genotyping shows C282Y homozygosity; H63D not detected. Ultrasound 4/30: hepatomegaly, smooth contour, no focal lesion, normal spleen, no ascites.

Plan:
1. Therapeutic phlebotomy, 500 mL weekly at our infusion center, beginning 5/12, with hemoglobin checked before each session. Target ferritin 50-100 ng/mL, then maintenance.
2. Avoid iron and vitamin C supplements and raw shellfish. Continue complete abstinence from alcohol.
3. First-degree relatives should be offered iron studies and HFE testing.
4. Fibrosis assessment at follow-up once iron depletion is under way.
5. Ferritin and liver tests can be drawn at your office every 6 to 8 weeks; please send results.

Sincerely,
Gastroenterology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here to go over the hemochromatosis diagnosis. GI letter, ultrasound and genotype reviewed with him. First phlebotomy last Tuesday went without trouble; second session is today after work. Fatigue unchanged so far. Joints still stiff in the mornings. Abdominal pain on and off, no worse. Taking metformin, colesevelam, ezetimibe, D3; acetaminophen a few times a week. Has not taken any iron or vitamin C. He has told his brother, who plans to raise it with his own doctors.

O: vitals per flowsheet. Bronze tint to the skin, as GI described. Sclerae anicteric. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, liver edge palpable below the right costal margin, nontender, no ascites. No edema. Hands without synovitis.

A/P
1. Hereditary hemochromatosis (C282Y homozygous) with arthropathy and liver involvement. Phlebotomy per GI. We will draw ferritin and liver tests here every 6-8 weeks and send to GI. Problem list updated: inflammatory arthropathy folded into hemochromatosis arthropathy; liver disease now attributed to iron overload.
2. Acetaminophen: fine for joint pain, but keep to no more than 2 g a day (4 tablets) given the liver.
3. Type 2 diabetes: continue metformin; A1c with the July draw.
4. FH: continue ezetimibe and colesevelam.
5. Supplements: vitamin D ok. No multivitamin with iron, no vitamin C.
Labs in July. RTC with the September physical.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Optometry -- diabetic eye examination. Date of exam 6/25/2026.

Patient with type 2 diabetes since 2025. Visual acuity 20/20 OD, 20/20 OS with correction. Pupils equal and reactive. Intraocular pressures 15 OD, 16 OS. Dilated fundus exam: optic nerves healthy, maculae flat, no hemorrhages, microaneurysms or exudates in either eye.

Impression: no diabetic retinopathy. Repeat dilated exam in one year.
